content:
As Apple continues the extended testing periods for macOS Sonoma 14.8.8 and macOS Sequoia 15.7.8, the company is now rolling out the seventh Release Candidate for both systems. Here's what's new.

New Release Candidates now available

Four days ago, Apple rolled out the sixth release candidates for macOS Sonoma 14.8.8 and macOS Sequoia 15.7.8, alongside the first release candidates for macOS 26.6 and its counterpart.

Given the timing and number of release candidates, it would be natural to assume these were the final testing builds before official release. That turns out not to be the case.

Today, Apple has released the seventh release candidates for macOS Sonoma 14.8.8 and macOS Sequoia 15.7.8, bearing the following build numbers:

  • macOS Sonoma 14.8.8 (23J620)
  • macOS Sequoia 15.7.8 (24G824)

Both builds are now available for download by developers and public beta testers.

Apple has not yet elaborated on what these two systems contain, only noting as usual that "this update provides important security fixes and is recommended for all users." Apple will likely provide more details on its Apple security updates page after both systems are officially released.

Apple has consistently issued updates for older system versions, delivering important bug fixes for users unable to run the latest software. This situation is believed to be no exception, so anyone still using macOS Sonoma or Sequoia should install the update as soon as it becomes publicly available, which is expected to happen as early as the beginning of next week.
